sonnet.problem: Card 12 already asked who is behind the man's sorrow (God's indignation and wrath), and the answer comes from the same verse (10). Card 13 asks the same point again as a true/false about who picked him up and cast him aside. The card 12 answer also gives the card 13 answer away.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question.

sonnet.problem: Card 17 jokes "I get proud of ONE good batch" against God's creation. Card 19 uses the same joke shape: Papa Dorin's small, worn-out self next to God's vast works ("I wore out on one kitchen counter, and He outlasts the HEAVENS"). That is the same comparison and punchline shape twice in one lesson, and it is not a callback that adds something new.
sonnet.rule: Each joke idea, comparison and punchline shape is used once per lesson. A callback is the one exception, and it adds something new.
